messages:
jamie: Thinking about a hedge strategy for our preemptible GPU pools — want to avoid full double-reserve but still keep tail latency bounded. Any thoughts on using taint annotations + quorum-based eviction delays?
ricardo: +1. We tried simple weighted fallback before but saw flapping during AZ-wide interruptions. Quorum delay might dampen churn.
sasha: Can you sketch the flow? I want to make sure it interacts well with cluster-autoscaler and our rollout hooks.
jamie: Idea: annotate nodes with `preemptible-group=<id>` and `preemptible-quorum=n`. When an interrupt webhook fires for a node, it broadcasts to a small coordinator which checks how many other nodes in the group are also interrupting. If below quorum, we delay eviction (extend TTL) and mark node `taint=preemptible-delayed:NoExecute` so pods that tolerate can stay.
kira: How do we extend TTL without breaking cloud termination notice behavior? infra-bot: cloudwatch-hook: termination-notice for instance i-0a1b2c arrived; STS=120s.
ricardo: The webhook can't stop provider termination, but we can use a short graceful window for app-level shutdown and move eviction off critical paths. e.g., from the 120s we use first 30s to attempt local checkpointing, then 60s to migrate tolerant pods, last 30s to force-evict.
sasha: We need cluster-autoscaler changes: it must respect `preemptible-delay` annotation so it doesn't immediately replace nodes causing oscillation. Also autoscaler should prefer heterogenous groups (reserve small guaranteed pool) rather than immediate scale-up to expensive on-demand.
jamie: Example annotation set we discussed:
```
node.annotations:
  redwood.com/preemptible-group: "gpu-fleet-3"
  redwood.com/preemptible-quorum: "2"
  redwood.com/preemptible-delay-seconds: "45"
```
ricardo: For taints/tolerations: critical system pods should have `tolerations: [{key: "preemptible-delayed", operator: "Exists", effect: "NoExecute"}]`. Non-tolerant pods will be evicted immediately once delay expires.
kira: What about cost tradeoffs? Delaying eviction longer increases probability we'll need on-demand replacements later, but reduces churn for stateful training jobs. We should expose a knob per customer/workload.
sasha: Ops checklist: 1) implement interrupt coordinator (lightweight TTL store, maybe leaderless via etcd/consul); 2) webhook to annotate/delay and emit events; 3) CA patch to honor annotation and backoff replacements; 4) update lifecycle hooks to run checkpoint daemonset.
jamie: Also consider mixed-capacity pools with gradation: 20% reserved (on-demand), 60% preemptible with quorum protection, 20% spot-burst for scale. That kept costs down in the sim.
ricardo: Let's prototype coordinator as a sidecar + a ConfigMap-based lock so we avoid extra infra. If too chatty we can move to redis.
ira-bot: NOTE: scheduled maintenance in us-west1 next week might increase interruptions; recommend testing there first.
kira: :thumbsup: I'll put a short RFC and include rough SLA impact numbers and cost delta.
jamie: Thanks — I'll run a small cluster simulation to estimate tail latency change and share results.
sasha: If anyone wants to pair on autoscaler changes ping me.
ricardo: I'll mock the webhook and run local e2e.
jamie: OK closing here, will post RFC link when ready.
